exercises.title: U1 听力·对话 Before the Big Test
exercises.speaker: uk_female
transcript: Mia: You look really tired today, Sam. Are you all right?
Sam: Not really. I have a big maths test tomorrow and I can't stop worrying.
Mia: I know that feeling. My hands always go cold and sweaty before a test.
Sam: Mine too. Last night I couldn't sleep at all.
Mia: Have you tried taking a few short breaks while you study?
Sam: No. I just study for hours until my head aches.
Mia: That makes it worse. Try a ten-minute break every hour and breathe slowly.
Sam: That sounds simple. I'll give it a try tonight.
Mia: And remember, a little stress is normal. It can even help you focus.
exercises.translation_cn: Mia 发现 Sam 很累;Sam 明天有数学大考,担心得睡不着;Mia 也会考前手脚冰冷出汗;Mia 建议学习时每小时休息十分钟并慢慢呼吸;Sam 决定试试;Mia 提醒一点压力是正常的,还能帮助集中注意力。

options: He decides to try it that night.

exercises.title: U1 听力·短文 Good Stress and Bad Stress
exercises.speaker: uk_female
transcript: Not all stress is bad for you.
Good stress shows up when you are called on in class or give a report.
A small amount of it can even help you prepare well.
Bad stress happens when worried feelings last for a long time.
That kind of stress can make you sick if you do not deal with it.
exercises.translation_cn: 并非所有压力都是坏的;被点名回答或做报告时出现的是好压力;少量好压力甚至能帮你做好准备;当担忧持续很久时就成了坏压力;如果不加处理,坏压力会让你生病。

questions.stem: What is the passage mainly about?
options: How to pass a maths test.
The difference between good and bad stress.

questions.stem: When might good stress show up?
options: When you are called on or give a report.

questions.stem: What can a small amount of good stress do?
options: Make you feel ill at once.

questions.stem: When does stress become bad?
options: When it lasts only one minute.
When it happens before a party.
When the worried feelings last a long time.

questions.stem: What can bad stress do if you ignore it?
options: It can give you more friends.

exercises.title: U1 听力·对话 A Visit to the Counsellor
exercises.speaker: uk_female
transcript: Counsellor: Come in, Leo. You said you wanted to talk about something?
Leo: Yes. Lately I feel anxious all the time, even when nothing is wrong.
Counsellor: I see. Do you have trouble sleeping or paying attention?
Leo: Both. I keep checking my homework again and again.
Counsellor: Thank you for being honest. Admitting it is already a brave first step.
Leo: So what can I do?
Counsellor: Let's start with a balanced plan: enough sleep, some exercise, and time to relax.
Leo: That sounds manageable.
Counsellor: And if the worry stays too strong, we can talk again or see a doctor.
exercises.translation_cn: 心理老师请 Leo 进来谈话;Leo 说最近总是焦虑,哪怕没出事;他睡不好、注意力差,还反复检查作业;老师肯定他的坦诚,说承认问题已是勇敢的第一步;建议从平衡作息开始:充足睡眠、适当运动、留出放松时间;若担忧仍太强,可再谈或看医生。

exercises.title: U1 听力·短文 A Quick Way to Calm Down
exercises.speaker: uk_female
transcript: Here is a quick way to calm down when you feel panicky.
Breathe in slowly through your nose and then breathe out through your mouth.
You can do this anywhere, and no one will even notice.
Listening to gentle music or doing some yoga also helps.
Choose the one that works for you and practise it often.
exercises.translation_cn: 给你一个惊慌时快速平静下来的方法:用鼻子慢慢吸气,再用嘴呼气;这随时随地都能做,没人会察觉;听轻柔的音乐或做点瑜伽也有帮助;选一个适合自己的方法并经常练习。

options: When you want to run fast.

exercises.title: U1 听力·对话 Planning a Balanced Weekend
exercises.speaker: uk_female
transcript: Emma: You've been studying all week, Jack. What are your plans for the weekend?
Jack: More study, I suppose. I have so much to finish.
Emma: That sounds stressful. You really need a balanced weekend.
Jack: What do you mean by balanced?
Emma: Keep your SELF in mind: Sleep, Exercise, Leisure and Food.
Jack: So I shouldn't just sit at my desk the whole time?
Emma: Exactly. Sleep well, go for a run, see your friends, and eat properly.
Jack: When you put it like that, it makes sense.
Emma: A rested mind works far better than a tired one anyway.
exercises.translation_cn: Emma 问 Jack 周末计划;Jack 说还想继续学习;Emma 说那太累了,他需要平衡的周末;她解释 SELF:睡眠、运动、休闲、饮食;建议别整天坐书桌前,要好好睡、去跑步、见朋友、好好吃饭;Jack 觉得有道理;Emma 说休息好的大脑比疲惫的大脑高效得多。

exercises.title: U1 听力·短文 Talking Helps
exercises.speaker: uk_female
transcript: When something is worrying you, do not keep it all inside.
Talking to a parent or teacher you trust can really help.
Saying your worries out loud often makes them feel lighter.
A trusted adult may even have ideas you had not thought of.
Remember, asking for help is a sign of strength, not weakness.
